newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer on currency strength.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer on currency strength.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger in moderate trade on Wednesday as solid gains overnight by the Canadian dollar helped boost prices, dealers said.

"What's driving things is continued dollar strength, and the underlying tone of the U.S. bond market still seems to be pretty good," said one T-bill trader with a Toronto-based brokerage. "I think there was probably a little bit of foreign buying overnight."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.19 percent from 3.20 percent at Tuesday's close.

The Canadian dollar firmed in quiet overnight trading, strengthening as far as C$1.3920 (US$0.7184) from Tuesday's close of C$1.3952 (US$0.7167). The dollar had been a major source of concern for T-bill investors as it fell to two-year lows in recent weeks.
The trader said much of the activity in the T-bill market was dealers switching positions along the yield curve rather than buying by accounts.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.61 percent from 3.63 percent at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 4.19 percent, from 4.20 percent at Tuesday's close.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
